source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured primary references. Current Terraform documentation supports state-to-remote-object bindings, one-to-one ownership, remote storage/locking, plan snapshot semantics, create/update/replace/destroy actions, and sensitive state concerns. Current OpenTofu documentation supports lifecycle customization without being treated as a universal migration guarantee. Kubernetes documents namespace, RBAC, quota, network-policy, control-plane, and data-plane multi-tenancy boundaries. Crossplane documents composite APIs, compositions, revisions, desired-state pipelines, composed-resource authority, readiness, and deletion consequences. Current Google Cloud, AWS Organizations, and Azure landing-zone documentation supports durable hierarchy, institutional ownership, inherited policy, account/subscription separation, governance, identity, and management foundations.

evidence: Checked E=(O,P,R,I,N,C,D,Q,L), capability revision mapping, resource graph, dependency edges, binding injectivity, declared/state/remote drift function, saved-plan tuple, and readiness conjunction.
Checked tuple, function, graph, vertex/edge, membership, time index, hash/version fields, difference function, injectivity, and conjunction notation with GitHub-compatible delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates request intent, realized graph, resource identity, time-varying drift, point-in-time plans, and multi-dimensional readiness.

evidence: Executed environment-control-inventory and reproduced nine environments, three production, four ephemeral, five isolated-account, seven private-network, eight locked-state, eight drift-monitored, four destroy-protected, and nine cost-owned environments.
Manually summed each tier and control field across all nine rows and matched the executable output.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The inventory is synthetic and explicitly disclaims control effectiveness.

evidence: Expanded the nine-field environment request through ownership, purpose, region/failure policy, identity, network, control plane, data/dependencies, policy tier, and lifecycle.
Expanded capability realization into a versioned resource DAG and checked dependency meaning for creation, readiness, migration, and destruction.
Expanded binding ownership so distinct managed addresses cannot ambiguously own one remote object and competing controllers remain forbidden.
Expanded drift across declared configuration, recorded state, and remote observation as a policy classification rather than raw inequality.

Expanded plan authorization across configuration/input digest, state version, capability/provider versions, proposed actions, and time/expiry; expanded readiness across identity, network, control plane, dependencies, policy/quota, and observability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The model supports traceability and control decisions but does not claim provider or environment correctness.

evidence: Reviewed namespace versus control-plane/node/account isolation, employee-owned hierarchy, inherited-policy movement, shared-foundation outages, provider quota, public/private paths, and strict tenant boundaries.

Reviewed local/lost/sensitive state, broad state readers, concurrent and competing writers, imports/moves, stale screenshot plans, replacement/destruction, organization-admin credentials, malicious modules/providers, and partial provider outcomes.

Reviewed created-but-unusable resources, positive/negative conformance vantage points, provider normalization, emergency drift, unauthorized exposure, revision-driven database replacement, correlated automatic upgrades, and tool ownership transfer.
Reviewed preview TTL leaks, external DNS/snapshots, real-data misuse, destroy-versus-state removal, dependency/data/legal holds, transfer, identity revocation, cost closure, and tombstone reuse.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Isolation, hierarchy, state, plan, authority, provider, conformance, drift, revision, ephemerality, migration, and deletion boundaries are explicit.

evidence: Traced environment ownership, purpose, tier, geography, cost, creation, expiry/review, and deletion authority from request through catalog tombstone.
Checked governed parentage and stable intent API across landing-zone foundation, isolation selection, composition, outputs, extensions, and provider changes.
Checked single writer/binding, protected remote state, plan freshness, short-lived scoped credentials, serialized apply, checkpoints, and audit across execution and migration.

Checked tiered controls, conformance-based readiness, classified drift, revision canaries/adoption, TTL enforcement, dependency-aware deprovisioning, evidence/data retention, authority revocation, and cost closure across examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: All declared ownership, hierarchy, API, binding, state, plan, authority, readiness, drift, revision, and deletion invariants remain consistent.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof; equations model a conditional provisioning assurance structure.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; provider, module/plugin, state, credential, policy, conformance, and requirements assumptions are explicit.

evidence: The executable control inventory is labeled synthetic and disclaims real control operation.
Worked hierarchy, state, provider, drift, preview, migration, and deletion cases are framed as scenarios rather than observed incidents.
Official tool/provider behavior, durable platform design guidance, formal models, and measurements to collect remain distinguishable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external infrastructure plan, cloud account, conformance test, drift scan, migration, teardown, security review, or production result is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats provisioning as a versioned lifecycle and authority product, preserving distinctions among environment and namespace, configuration/state/remote reality, planning/apply, existence/conformance, drift/incident, state removal/destruction, and ephemerality/low criticality.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can define the product contract, select isolation, establish landing zones, expose composed APIs, protect state/plans/credentials, reconcile partial outcomes, test conformance, govern drift, design tiers, migrate revisions/controllers, and deprovision with closure.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from environment product and isolation through hierarchy, API, composition, state, plans, authority, partial outcomes, conformance, drift, tiers, revisions, deprovisioning, and operations. Ten examples cover boundary selection, hierarchy, plan races, readiness, emergency drift, destructive revisions, TTL leakage, ambiguous timeouts, controller transfer, and lifecycle closure. Five exercises progress from definitions through lifecycle tracing, diagnosis, tier design, and fleet migration, with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
